sections.html:
Talbot County sits in west central Georgia, with Talbotton as the county seat and largest city. It covers 395 square miles, 391 of them land, and was founded on December 14, 1827 and named for Matthew Talbot, according to Wikipedia's county entry, which draws its area numbers from the Census Bureau.

The county straddles the fall line, so the north is hillier than the south. The far northern edge belongs to the Pine Mountain range, where the highest peaks pass 1,000 feet, and the Fall Line Freeway follows State Route 96 across the southern part from Geneva to Junction City. U.S. 80 and State Route 22 run through as well, and two rail lines cross the county: a CSX subdivision and the Norfolk Southern Columbus District.

Besides Talbotton, the incorporated places are Woodland, Geneva, Junction City and a part of Manchester, with Box Springs as a census-designated place. Po Biddy Crossroads, Tax Crossroads and Centerville are unincorporated. Upson, Taylor, Marion, Chattahoochee, Muscogee, Harris and Meriwether counties form the border. The Census Bureau estimates 5,709 residents for July 2025, spread across 391 land square miles, or about 15 people per square mile.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Talbot County homes?
sections.html:
Talbot County is a small ownership market: 79.6% of housing units are owner-occupied, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $117,100 for 2020-2024. The table collects the main figures from the Census Bureau.

Zero building permits in 2025 and a 42.9 minute average commute describe a place where residents often work in other counties and almost no new housing is being added. Nearly three in ten residents are 65 or older, so many homes here pass through estates. An heir who inherits a house with unpaid taxes meets the tax commissioner's rules before a buyer does.

sections.h2: Where do I go for Talbot County property tax questions?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner's office is at 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 147, Talbotton, GA 31827. Its website lists hours of 8:00 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday, closed for lunch from 12:00 to 1:00, and the phone numbers 706-665-3240 and 706-665-3280.

  • Tax commissioner: bills, payments, mobile home titles, timber tax and tax sales.
  • Tax assessors, 706-665-3377: values, returns, exemption applications and appeals.
  • Board of Commissioners, 35 Madison St., 706-665-3220: the mobile home location permit.
  • Clerk of Superior Court: collects the intangible tax on recorded security instruments.

Payment can be made by cash, check, money order, Visa, MasterCard or Discover, and the office says a convenience fee is added to card payments. The parcel search runs through qPublic.

sections.h2: When are Talbot County taxes due, and how do late charges work?
sections.html:
Real and personal property bills are generally mailed in October and due December 20. The commissioner's property tax page says partial payments are accepted, and that after the due date interest accrues at prime plus 3% with a 5% penalty added every 120 days up to 20%.

Mobile homes follow a separate calendar. Their bills are generally mailed in January and are due April 1, and every mobile home must display a current decal, which is handed over when the tax is paid. Owners of a mobile home located in the county on January 1 must return it for taxation on or before April 1, and a missed return carries a 10% penalty.

One local item appears next to the tax notices on the commissioner's site. A garbage collection fee rose to $225.00 per year on January 1, 2026, with extra carts at $137.00 per year. Ask the office whether that fee sits on your tax account so the closing agent includes it.

sections.h2: How does a Talbot County tax sale work?
sections.html:
The tax commissioner runs levy sales for unpaid state, county and school taxes under Title 48 and Title 9 of the Georgia code. Properties are advertised in the Talbotton New Era for four consecutive weeks, and the sale takes place on the first Tuesday of the month after the final week of advertising.

  • Sales run between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse, 26 South Washington Avenue.
  • The county does not guarantee title, and the buyer has no use of the property and no right to rent for at least one year under Georgia law.
  • Winning bidders pay in cash or certified funds right after the sale.
  • Money left after taxes and costs becomes excess funds, claimed by written request to the commissioner at 38 South Jefferson Avenue.

The office also posts a guide to the right of redemption. A homeowner who is behind has a window to act, and a cash sale before the levy can leave more equity than waiting for an auction.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Talbot County value or claim an exemption?
sections.html:
A property owner who disagrees with the appraised value on an assessment notice files with the Board of Assessors, and the first written dispute must name the method of appeal. The commissioner's general information page lists four: Board of Equalization, Superior Court, arbitration or hearing officer. The state revenue department's county sheet says the appeal must be postmarked within 45 days of the notice's mailing date.

Real estate returns go to the tax assessors between January 1 and April 1 when property has changed or been acquired, and failing to file a required return costs a 10% penalty on the value not returned. Personal property returns on form PT-50P are due every year by April 1.

The commissioner's site gives April 1 as the last day to apply for homestead and other exemptions for the current year, and an application received later takes effect the next year. The state sheet lists no local homestead exemptions for Talbot County, so the statewide ones apply. Once granted, the exemption renews itself until you move or the ownership changes.

sections.h2: What should a seller do about Talbot County taxes?
sections.html:
Ask the commissioner for a written payoff on each open year, including mobile home and timber accounts if they apply. If the house was inherited, ask which years are unpaid before you list, since a recorded lien must be cleared at closing.

Refunds are limited. A claim for taxes paid in error must be filed in writing with the Board of Commissioners within three years of payment, and the commissioner's page says refunds rest on errors of fault, not on disagreements over value. That makes the January 1 ownership date and your closing statement the places where a sale gets settled between buyer and seller.

With almost no new construction and slow turnover, Talbot County listings can sit. A direct cash buyer who takes the house as it is can pay the open balance from the proceeds at the table.

faqs.q: Where is the Talbot County tax commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 38 South Jefferson Avenue in Talbotton, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 147. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 4:30 pm and closes for lunch from 12:00 to 1:00.

faqs.q: When are Talbot County property taxes due?
faqs.a: December 20 for real and personal property, with bills generally mailed in October. Mobile home bills are mailed in January and due April 1.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial payment on Talbot County taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The commissioner's page says partial payments are accepted, though interest and penalties keep running on the unpaid portion after the due date.

faqs.q: When are Talbot County tax levy sales held?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of a month, after four consecutive weeks of newspaper advertising in the Talbotton New Era. They take place at the courthouse on South Washington Avenue between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Talbot County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: April 1 of the year the exemption is first claimed. The commissioner's FAQ says applications can be submitted at any time, but later ones apply to the next year.
